literature_notes: HEPACAM (GlialCAM) is a single-pass type I transmembrane protein: extracellular ectodomain residues 34–240, TM 241–261, intracellular tail 262–416. Every ledger line (L1–L7) describes a C-terminal tag — either 3×FLAG (L1–L4) or HA (L5–L7) — appended after the final residue 416, which lies in the cytoplasmic tail. The naming conventions 'GlialCAM-FLAG', 'hepaCAM-FLAG', 'hepaCAM-HA', and 'pcDNA3.1-hepaCAM-HA' all follow the protein-name-then-tag convention for C-terminal fusions, and no ledger line places any tag on the extracellular N-terminus (mature residue 34) or anywhere within the ectodomain (34–240). L6 mentions 'HA immunolabeling' to assess localization, but this is consistent with permeabilized-cell staining or with 'surface' meaning 'at cell–cell junctions' (as in L2 for the FLAG construct); it does not relocate the HA tag to the extracellular face. No ledger line reports an insertion tolerated on the extracellular face of HEPACAM. Zero sites qualify.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal 3×FLAG tag on full-length GlialCAM/HEPACAM; residue 416 is in the intracellular tail (topology 262–416); construct traffics to cell–cell junctions but the tag faces the cytoplasm.
C-terminal FLAG tag on shRNA-resistant human hepaCAM used for astrocyte morphogenesis rescue; residue 416 is intracellular.
